# One-way ANOVA with a UQ Brush-turkey Study {.title-slide}

## Teaching demonstration

Does incubation temperature change the average time until hatching for Australian Brush-turkey eggs?

![](../images/brush_turkey_scene.png){width="48%"}

---

## Research context and UQ connection

- Study: Eiby and Booth (2009), *Journal of Comparative Physiology B*.
- Authors: Yvonne A. Eiby and David T. Booth, School of Biological Sciences, The University of Queensland.
- Eggs came from brush-turkeys breeding on UQ's St Lucia campus.

Reference: Eiby, Y. A., & Booth, D. T. (2009). The effects of incubation temperature on the morphology and composition of Australian Brush-turkey (*Alectura lathami*) chicks. *Journal of Comparative Physiology B*, 179, 875--882. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00360-009-0370-4

---

## Data provenance

The data are reconstructed integer incubation periods that reproduce the published group means and standard errors. The per-egg values are not the authors' original observations.

---

## Load the CSV

```{webr}
csv_paths <- c(
  "brushturkey_incubation.csv",
  "data/brushturkey_incubation.csv",
  "../data/brushturkey_incubation.csv"
)
csv_path <- csv_paths[file.exists(csv_paths)][1]
bt <- read.csv(csv_path)
bt$temperature <- factor(bt$temperature, levels = c(32, 34, 36))

head(bt)
table(bt$temperature)
```

---

## Plotly boxplots: no points, no zoom

The boxplot below is drawn with Plotly in the browser. It shows only boxes and whiskers; individual points are hidden and zoom/crop controls are disabled.

<div id="bt-plotly-boxplot" class="plotly-chart"></div>

<script>
(function(){
  function loadPlotly(callback) {
    if (window.Plotly) { callback(); return; }
    const script = document.createElement("script");
    script.src = "https://cdn.plot.ly/plotly-2.25.2.min.js";
    script.onload = callback;
    document.head.appendChild(script);
  }
  function parseCsv(text) {
    const lines = text.trim().split(/\r?\n/);
    const header = lines.shift().split(",");
    return lines.map(line => {
      const parts = line.split(",");
      const row = {};
      header.forEach((h, i) => row[h] = parts[i]);
      row.temperature = Number(row.temperature);
      row.incubation_period = Number(row.incubation_period);
      return row;
    });
  }
  async function drawBrushTurkeyBoxplot() {
    const div = document.getElementById("bt-plotly-boxplot");
    if (!div) return;
    const response = await fetch("../data/brushturkey_incubation.csv");
    const rows = parseCsv(await response.text());
    const temps = [32, 34, 36];
    const traces = temps.map(t => ({
      type: "box",
      name: t + " °C",
      y: rows.filter(d => d.temperature === t).map(d => d.incubation_period),
      boxpoints: false,
      hoverinfo: "y+name",
      line: { width: 2 },
      marker: { opacity: 0 }
    }));
    const layout = {
      margin: { l: 72, r: 22, t: 18, b: 64 },
      paper_bgcolor: "white",
      plot_bgcolor: "white",
      dragmode: false,
      xaxis: { title: "Incubation temperature (°C)", fixedrange: true, zeroline: false },
      yaxis: { title: "Incubation period (days)", fixedrange: true, zeroline: false, range: [40, 55] },
      showlegend: false
    };
    const config = {
      displayModeBar: false,
      scrollZoom: false,
      doubleClick: false,
      responsive: true
    };
    Plotly.newPlot(div, traces, layout, config);
  }
  document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function(){ loadPlotly(drawBrushTurkeyBoxplot); });
})();
</script>

```{webr}
csv_paths <- c(
  "brushturkey_incubation.csv",
  "data/brushturkey_incubation.csv",
  "../data/brushturkey_incubation.csv"
)
csv_path <- csv_paths[file.exists(csv_paths)][1]
bt <- read.csv(csv_path)
bt$temperature <- factor(bt$temperature, levels = c(32, 34, 36))

aggregate(incubation_period ~ temperature, data = bt, summary)
```

## One-way ANOVA

```{webr}
csv_paths <- c(
  "brushturkey_incubation.csv",
  "data/brushturkey_incubation.csv",
  "../data/brushturkey_incubation.csv"
)
csv_path <- csv_paths[file.exists(csv_paths)][1]
bt <- read.csv(csv_path)
bt$temperature <- factor(bt$temperature, levels = c(32, 34, 36))

fit <- aov(incubation_period ~ temperature, data = bt)
summary(fit)
```

---

## Post hoc comparisons

```{webr}
csv_paths <- c(
  "brushturkey_incubation.csv",
  "data/brushturkey_incubation.csv",
  "../data/brushturkey_incubation.csv"
)
csv_path <- csv_paths[file.exists(csv_paths)][1]
bt <- read.csv(csv_path)
bt$temperature <- factor(bt$temperature, levels = c(32, 34, 36))
fit <- aov(incubation_period ~ temperature, data = bt)

TukeyHSD(fit)
```

---

## Assumption and robustness checks

```{webr}
csv_paths <- c(
  "brushturkey_incubation.csv",
  "data/brushturkey_incubation.csv",
  "../data/brushturkey_incubation.csv"
)
csv_path <- csv_paths[file.exists(csv_paths)][1]
bt <- read.csv(csv_path)
bt$temperature <- factor(bt$temperature, levels = c(32, 34, 36))
fit <- aov(incubation_period ~ temperature, data = bt)

shapiro.test(residuals(fit))
oneway.test(incubation_period ~ temperature, data = bt, var.equal = FALSE)
kruskal.test(incubation_period ~ temperature, data = bt)
```

---

## Takeaway

The ANOVA shows strong evidence that mean incubation period differs by temperature. The main practical difference is between 32 °C and the two warmer groups.
